corrections: Both native descriptor selectors use unsigned comparisons and fall back to descriptor zero for out-of-range IDs; they do not reject invalid IDs.
Removing the slot-18 skip changes original behavior. The inspected original does not establish that this skip is a bug.
The original action counter increments only for visible rows. Action 338 is possible after removing the skip, but is not an original hidden-row action.
Runtime descriptor counts, artwork tokens, appearance reports and mod regression results were not independently reproduced and do not validate recovered original behavior.

findings.hint: Recover the 93-byte native setter at [0x448830,0x44888D). Preserve unsigned descriptor-zero fallback, descriptor assignment and visual refresh/refcount effects. No implementation or registry entry was found in the searched reference recovery files; PE-MENU-RELOCATIONS.md contains existing prologue evidence only.
evidence: Original objdump shows ECX as this, one stack DWORD argument and RET 4 at 0x44888A. INT3 padding follows; the next prologue starts at 0x448890.
0x448833 loads the UI singleton from 0x00BFBAA4. CMP/JB selects UI+12 plus ID*100 when unsigned ID < [UI+16], otherwise UI+12.
0x44884F loads [this+0x184]; 0x448857 writes its +4 descriptor pointer even when its visual pointer at +0 is null.
For a nonnull visual, instructions increment its reference count through the vtable-derived adjustment, call 0x48B8F0, then call 0x41F500 with this+0x174 bit 0.
dependencies: UI singleton 0x00BFBAA4; descriptor base +12 and count +16
Owned record at this+0x184; visual pointer +0 and descriptor pointer +4
Visual vtable adjustment and reference-count layout
validation_plan: Compare original and candidate with synthetic descriptor tables for IDs 0, count-1, count and 0xFFFFFFFF.
Exercise null and nonnull visual records and both flag-bit values; compare descriptor writes, refcounts and ordered call arguments.
Use original dependency implementations for integrated refresh tests and compare geometry and visual state before and after.
limits: The setter was fully disassembled; its two callees were not analyzed.
The native method name is attributed by the note; the inspected instructions independently establish its behavior.

findings.hint: Recover the factory separately at [0x422030,0x422178), including ownership and exception cleanup. Its descriptor-selection logic is a useful shared semantic component with the setter.
evidence: Original metadata lists the integer-ID createSprite overload as native unmanaged thiscall.
Disassembly shows ECX UI, four stack arguments, RET 16 at 0x422175, padding and a distinct next prologue at 0x422180.
Unsigned CMP/JB at 0x42205D selects descriptor zero on invalid IDs and otherwise uses a 100-byte stride.
The factory allocates 0x194 bytes through IAT 0x92D4B4, identified by original imports as operator new.
Descriptor floats +8/+12 supply constructor width/height. The routine applies UI fields +0x60/+0x68/+0x70, sets origin, clears flag bits with AND 0xF9 and appends a descriptor-bearing owned record.
Final cleanup decrements the temporary visual reference count and invokes virtual destruction when it reaches zero.
dependencies: Operator new import, SEH/unwind support and virtual destruction
validation_plan: Compare descriptor fallback, constructor arguments, returned object fields and ordered helper calls.
Exercise count boundaries, origin variants and differing UI transform fields.
Validate ownership and exception cleanup with original dependencies before claiming factory equivalence.
limits: No duplicate was found in searched recovered code or native registry.
Constructor inspection was partial; descriptor resource-token meanings were not independently established.
Allocation-failure and exception paths require further analysis and execution.

findings.hint: Use the verified IL as a larger UI reconstruction lead after recovering its smaller native dependencies. Preserve the original 38-row behavior, reel ownership and fault handlers.
evidence: Original metadata identifies method row 5098, token 0x060013EA. Raw bytes confirm a 12-byte fat header, 2095 code bytes, maxstack 12 and locals token 0x11001348.
Original code SHA-256 is 8e6d74034b695f1ec1cc3dfb9a2fd0fd785a9f342de0df10f1aa73cf37777354.
IL+0x1B3 bytes 071f123b1d050000 branch to IL_06D8 when index equals 18. The loop terminates at index 39, producing 38 row-construction iterations.
IL_0192..019B resets the reel SSP at Profile+420. IL_05ED..05F6 calls vector.push_back at Profile+472.
The action counter starts at 299 and increments after the skip branch; IL_05BC stores it at row+8.
The method includes nested fault handlers, reference increments/decrements, scrollbar-related branches and final font release before RET at IL_082E.

SSP reference counting, vector.push_back and C++ unwind destructors
Virtual UI calls and original layout data

review.summary: Approved as a 93-byte assembly reference for VA 0x448830, covering [0x448830, 0x44888D). The original selects descriptors using an unsigned comparison and falls back to descriptor zero for an out-of-range index; it does not reject the index. The attributed method name and callers remain unverified. Byte equality establishes assembly-reference evidence only, with zero source-recovery credit.
review.reason: Independent disassembly confirms both branch paths converge at RET 4, followed by three INT3 bytes and a distinct prologue at 0x448890. The transcription preserves the observed instructions, calls and ABI; assembling and linking it at the original VA produced an unmasked 93-byte match. Neither recorded assembly nor source coverage overlaps the span. The original executable hash and candidate hashes match the receipts. The two callees and indirect callers remain dependencies, and no behavioral execution or callee equivalence was established.
